title: Gemini 'pixel art' + Retro Diffusion pixel-art-fixer: grid recovery, 96 px SE sprite
question: Does pixel-art-fixer (grid recovery, 1 cell = 1 px) plus the E2 palette lock rescue Gemini pixel-art outputs, old (26 images) and new (SE illustration -> 'true pixel art ~96 px')?
method: fixlib.fix_sq = fixer detect + square-grid check by round-trip error; figure crop; native -> 96 px (nearest <12%, else k-centroid x8); pz.finish palette lock (palette.json) + lock2 (obi recovery, per-material lightness match). metrics.py (pixtools venv), s3_identity.py, Argon + Opus A/B vs the m96 master. Scripts in exp/2026-10-28_sw_gemini_fixer/scripts.
result: Fixer is exact on its fast path (8.00/5.12/10.24 px), but 15/26 baseline images went to arbitration, which usually mis-detects step_x by 2-12%. The square check won on 14/26 (round-trip error 7-10 -> ~2 on 8 px grids). Gemini never draws at the requested size: 82-347 art px figures on 3-14 px grids (scale to 96 = 0.28-1.17). The old outputs stay off-model (ssim_b .13-.26). New a1b (fixer, x0.38, lock) gives ssim_b .93 / dE 10.7 vs the illustration, against the master's .81 / 16.4 (master vs its warped geo src: .92 / 11.1). Passing the master as a reference (a2) hurt it: .74 / 18.2.
verdict: Grid tool: keep (always via fix_sq). As a master replacement: no. Both critics pick the master (face at 1x; dark seam noise, eye blobs). Port a1b's red sock tops, crossed collar and visible bun by hand if wanted.
